title: Cardiac radiofrequency ablation
what: Thin tubes are passed through a blood vessel in the groin up to the heart. The doctor finds the spot that causes the rhythm problem and burns it. There are no cuts on the chest.
why: For heart rhythm problems when medicines do not help, cause side effects, or when ablation is the better choice for you.
duration: the procedure usually takes 1 to 4 hours; the hospital stay is usually 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners and rhythm medicines. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Allergies to iodine, contrast dye, or medicines
If you are or might be pregnant
If you ever had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, a heart ultrasound, and sometimes a 24-hour ECG or a heart CT scan. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop any medicines on your own. The doctor will tell you in advance which to take and which to skip.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before, and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact times.

prepare.title: Groin area
prepare.text: Sometimes you are asked to shave the groin. Check with your clinic.

bring: All your ECG records, especially from attacks
Things for a hospital stay of 1 to 3 days
steps: You lie on a table, and sensors are stuck on your chest
A thin tube called an IV is put into a vein. You get a calming medicine, sometimes general anesthesia
The groin is numbed with an injection
Thin tubes are passed through a blood vessel to the heart, guided by X-rays
The doctor studies your heart rhythm, and sometimes starts an attack on purpose
The problem spot is burned with high-frequency current
The tubes are removed, and a tight bandage is put on the groin
feel: The numbing injection in the groin stings
You may feel your heart racing when an attack is started
During the burning, you may feel burning or pressure in your chest. Tell the doctor
Afterwards, you need to lie for a few hours without bending your leg
after: Usually you lie flat for a few hours, then you can get up
A bruise in the groin is common and safe
For about a week, do not lift heavy things or do sports
In the first weeks, skipped beats sometimes happen. Tell your doctor
Take medicines after the procedure exactly as your doctor says
red_flags: Bleeding from the puncture site or a growing lump in the groin: press on it and call emergency services
Chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting
Your leg turns cold, pale, or numb
Weakness in an arm or leg, or trouble speaking: call emergency services

faq.a: It is done through a blood vessel, with no cuts on the chest. It is usually done with local numbing and a calming medicine.

faq.q: Will the arrhythmia go away for good after ablation?
faq.a: Often yes, but it depends on the type of arrhythmia. Sometimes a second procedure is needed. Your doctor will explain your case.

reminders.text: Ablation tomorrow. Pack your ID, ECG records, and list of medicines. Eat and drink only until the times your clinic gave you.
